note: Thu 19 Nov 2026 07:xx SGT refresh, as of the Wed 18 Nov US close / Asia Wed (HK) / Tue (JP,KR,SG) close. The risk-off extended for a third session but decelerated sharply (S&P 500 -0.50% to 7303.98, following Mon -1.92% and Tue -1.03%; Dow -1.32% to 50089.71; Nasdaq roughly flat at -0.02% to 24322.71; Russell 2000 +0.51% to 2715.75, diverging positive; VIX -3.02% to 24.69). Wednesday's FOMC October 27-28 minutes confirmed a genuinely hawkish Fed: nearly all officials see a need for further hikes, a couple floated 50bp, and Waller argued the Fed may need a larger December move, hardening CME-implied Dec 9 hike odds to roughly 90-95% (with a ~15% tail on 50bp). Precious-metals miners were crushed (GDX -6.94%, SILJ -5.85%, SLVP -6.52%, AG -7.56%, HL -6.56%, PAAS -6.59%, NEM -6.84%) far more than bullion itself (GLD -2.48%, SLV -4.69%) -- an operating-leverage/beta unwind, not a bullion-demand collapse -- while oil fell sharply (WTI -3.57% to $82.94, Brent proxy -4.22% to $89.21) on dollar strength (DXY ~103.6-103.8, near 19-20 month highs; 10yr yield ~5.10%). Rare earths bucked the broader tape (MP Materials +5.22% to $36.68, Lynas +2.83% to A$12.37) on renewed US-China rare-earth trade-talk optimism, an insider-buying cluster and a fresh Needham Buy reinstatement on MP, ahead of today's (Thu 19 Nov) Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen trilateral. Crypto stayed pressured (BTC -3.92% to $62,353, Crypto Fear & Greed at 11/Extreme Fear for a sixth straight day, ~$240m single-day BTC spot-ETF outflows). Credit remains calm (HY OAS ~334bp, below its 10yr average ~383bp; IG OAS ~93bp), the key reason this still reads as a rates/dollar shock rather than a systemic event. All 40 universe calls plus the 9-ticker rare-earth basket refreshed this run.

macro.regime: Selloff sharply accelerates as a growth scare (Philly Fed plunge) meets a near-locked hawkish Fed; VIX fear spike confirms genuine risk-off
macro.narrative: Thursday's session was a sharp acceleration, not a calming, of the drawdown: the S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7175.83 on a fourth straight down day, with Nasdaq -2.25%, Dow -2.19% and Russell 2000 -2.18% (fully reversing its prior positive divergence), while VIX spiked 15.8% to 28.44 -- the sharpest fear move of this entire stretch. The proximate afternoon catalyst was Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut (ANT): the Nasdaq-100 rallied over 1% intraday before a broad 'sell the news' reversal into the close, as the IPO's pricing failed to resolve investors' AI-capex-math anxiety -- AI labs are estimated to generate roughly $150B/year in revenue against nearly $1T in annual hyperscaler capex. That equity-specific AI-ROI anxiety compounded with a genuine domestic growth scare: the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index collapsed to 6.3 (from 20.9, forecast 20.0, a six-month low) and jobless claims rose to 203K, both landing atop Wednesday's confirmed-hawkish FOMC October minutes (nearly all officials favoring further hikes, Dec 9 odds near 95%) -- a stagflationary cross-current where weak growth data cannot offset a Fed still anchored to above-target inflation. Gold (-1.76% to a 14-month low) and silver (-2.60%) extended declines with miners again amplifying the move (GDX -3.77%, SILJ -5.66%) on Fed-hike bets and a firm dollar, while Bitcoin stayed mired in its drawdown (-1.32% to $62,154, down ~24% over the past month) with ETF outflows continuing. The one clean positive divergence remains rare earths (MP +1.98%, Lynas +3.40%, both a third straight up day) on China's extension of its rare-earth export-control pause to January 10, 2027 ahead of the ongoing Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen summit, even as laggard Energy Fuels (-2.84%) shows the rally isn't universal.

byAssetClass.note: The fourth straight down session (S&P -2.02%) with VIX spiking 15.8% to 28.44, a failed Anthropic-IPO rally reversing into a broad afternoon selloff, and the Philly Fed's collapse to a six-month low together tip the equity read from neutral to modestly cautious.

Gold hit a 14-month low (-1.76%) and silver fell 2.60% with miners again amplifying losses (GDX -3.77%) on Fed-hike bets and a firm dollar; rare earths (MP +1.98%, Lynas +3.40%) remain the lone bright spot but aren't broad enough to offset bullion/base-metal weakness.

Bitcoin fell a further 1.32% to $62,154 (down ~24% over the past month) with the Fear & Greed Index near 11 (Extreme Fear) and cumulative 2026 spot-ETF outflows exceeding $2.5B -- the Anthropic-IPO-driven tech reversal spilled directly into crypto with no stabilizing catalyst.

The confirmed-hawkish FOMC minutes (Dec 9 hike odds ~95%) and 10-year yield near 5.08-5.09% keep long duration pressured, even as Thursday's own growth-scare data (Philly Fed plunge, claims up to 203K) and the VIX spike provide a partial flight-to-quality offset.

A reconfirmed hawkish Fed path combined with intensifying risk-off (VIX +15.8%) and safe-haven dollar demand continue to support holding dollar/cash ballast into today's Japan CPI, China LPR, and Friday's revised UoM sentiment data.
